scope: Read-only visual review of latest GUI scene006–009 and their actual action logs. No simulation, model inference, training or source edits.

observed_stages.observed: Hand approaches target; fingers close and bowl visibly lifts off table.
Bowl moves over plate and descends to it.
Arm lingers close to bowl on plate with closed fingers; On is not yet a release.
Fingers open and hand retracts upward; bowl remains visibly on plate through final frame.

visual_review.inference: Successful released placement is supported by visible separation plus actual gap/distance. There is a placement dwell even in this positive-offset successful run.

contact_assessment.target_contact: Visible off-table lift/co-motion supports interaction with target; exact finger contact occluded.
contact_assessment.external_collision: No clearly visible collision blocking motion in sampled frames; contact forces not recorded.

observed_stages.observed: Gripper closes around target and visibly lifts it. It is not an empty-hand-only attempt.
Raised bowl traverses toward plate but remains visibly above and to its right; does not descend onto plate.
Hand and bowl move much more slowly while closed; bowl shifts to right of plate and lowers only partway.
Bowl remains suspended, hand remains near and closed, and pair drifts farther right/back away from plate. Final plate is empty; no release visible.

visual_review.inference: Main near-stop occurs after acquiring and transporting the bowl, around step150. Output XYZ magnitudes drop markedly along with actual motion, so an explanation consisting only of strong movement commands blocked by a collision is unsupported. External contact cannot be excluded from this single camera. Later drift is directed away from the required placement rather than completing descent.

contact_assessment.target_contact: Off-table bowl co-motion visible; no obvious table drop in sampled frames. This does not prove secure contact or exclude small slip.
contact_assessment.external_collision: At slowdown onset there is no unambiguous external impact visible. Late approach to cabinet is partially occluded; external contact/force status is unknown.

observed_stages.observed: Open hand slowly approaches target in cluster; brief closing attempts reopen, bowl stays near table until later.
Hand closes and raises target bowl, then transports it briskly toward right side above plate region.

visual_review.inference: Two slow phases exist: extended approach/acquisition and a stronger transport-to-placement near-stop around step300. XYZ output itself becomes small in later phase. This is neither a simulation frozen at initial approach nor proof of a physically blocked strong command.

contact_assessment.external_collision: No definite collision can be identified from sampled single-camera frames. Late proximity to cabinet may occlude contact; status unknown.

conclusions: Scene006/007 visibly release the bowl on plate and retreat. Scene007 has a small negative relative dx but positive absolute X; a literal any-negative-offset rule is not supported.

Scene008/009 both pick up the bowl. Their dominant late failure is carrying above/to the side of plate, producing small XYZ commands and slowly drifting away without placing/releasing, not a uniform empty grasp. Scene009 additionally has a slow approach.
008 slowdown around150: mean XYZ command norm .366→.0628 and actual consecutive-post EEF movement4.90→.591mm/step. 009 slowdown around300: .230→.0633 and3.085→.553mm/step.
These are new negativeX/positiveY scenes, independently inspected. Earlier negativeX/negativeY conclusions were not substituted.
Logged actions do not show strong translation continuing against an immovable contact as a complete explanation; force/contact data are absent, so collision is not ruled out.
limitations: Only256x256 dynamic agentview video is saved; wrist image is initial only. Fingers/bowl/cabinet contact can be occluded.
Interactive GUI trials have advancing policy RNG across resets and possible untracked native GUI edits, as recorded in scene metadata; they are not a fully controlled sign-ablation experiment.
Video10FPS is half of the nominal20Hz control rate; step labels refer to completed controlsteps, frame0 initial.
CSV next pre-state and previous post_eef differ slightly. Temporal motion statistics here use consecutive post_eef positions, not post-minus-pre; no controller state was reconstructed.
Command norm change is an observable output property; it does not on its own identify dataset coverage, model reasoning, collision causes, or the training fix needed.
On/done alone is not treated as complete placement. Actual opening, EEF-bowl separation, and visual stability are checked separately.
